# Review Fixes

All six correctness issues reproduced during the 2026-08-27 review are fixed
in this checkout. Their nine reproductions now live in `tests/regressions/`
and must pass with Typst 0.15.1. This page retains its original URL for
existing links and records the behavior changes; it is not an inventory of
outstanding failures.

## Font-relative geometry {#font-relative-geometry}

Geometric `em` components now resolve against surrounding text before zoom,
clipping, polygon validation, port projection, or bounds arithmetic. Node
minima/insets/radii, gate size/spacing, stroke thickness, edge label/highlight
geometry, and decorative parts/marks all use this boundary. Manual
`.to-absolute()` workarounds are no longer needed:

```typ
#set text(size: 10pt)
#typ.diagram(scale: 2, typ.edge(
  typ.node(0, 0, style: (shape: typ.shapes.diamond, min-size: 2em)),
  (2, 0), stroke: 0.1em + black,
))
```

Absolute-only, unlabeled geometry helpers remain usable without `context`.
Mixed-sign dimensions are checked again after resolution; negative sizes
still fail. Custom extension fields remain the builder's responsibility.
See [Font-relative lengths](../reference/diagram.qmd#font-relative-lengths).

## Highlight bounds at acute joins

Bounds now include the maximum offset-centerline displacement **and** the
band stroke's miter extension. Single-segment curves receive the same
allowance because their highlights are sampled into polylines. Rendering and
bounds share the two miter limits, so changing one cannot silently invalidate
the other. These conservative bounds can add whitespace around highlighted
joins; they are not a pixel-tight ink crop.

## Square-capped diagonal wire bounds

Open square-capped wires now reserve up to `sqrt(2)` times half their stroke
thickness on each axis, covering a diagonal cap's tangent and normal
projections. Miter allowance can enlarge this further. Butt/round caps and
closed node outlines retain their existing bounds.

## Automatic config values {#automatic-config-values}

Passing `auto` now inherits the enclosing config value, including for
`node-styles` and `edge-styles`. Without an enclosing value, the package
default applies. Two existing meaningful automatic values are preserved:
`font-size: auto` restores surrounding document text sizing and
`baseline: auto` restores the calculated baseline. Use concrete values such
as `scale: 1` to reset other keys. Nested scopes still restore their parent.

## Zero-sized built-in polygons

Built-in polygon builders supply a `1pt` fitting fallback for any zero axis,
before applying their template's proportions and rotation. This preserves a
valid outline when no label, inset, or minimum supplies an extent. Explicit
nonzero dimensions remain unchanged. Custom polygon validity checks remain
strict. Use `shapes.empty` when an invisible routing point is intended.

## Circle fitting for box-like labels

The circle radius now contains the farthest corner of the measured label
rectangle, including shifts from asymmetric padding. Larger explicit minima
and the existing 1.2-axis clearance still win. A `20pt` square therefore gets
a radius of approximately `14.14pt`, not `12pt`; thin labels that already fit
are unchanged. Unlabeled zero-size circles stay zero-sized.
